messages.subject: Filtering out abiotic frequency peaks - fpeaks() - rain, wind
messages.subject_clean: Filtering out abiotic frequency peaks - fpeaks() - rain, wind
messages.body_plain:
Hello sage seewave community:

Drawing from results from the fpeaks() function, I am interested in isolating only the frequency peaks generated by animals, and am looking for advice on filtering out the abiotic fraction of the soundscape (primarily, rain and wind).

Are there seewave-based techniques that folks have used to successfully flag recordings with instances of rain or wind and/or filter out corresponding frequency peaks generated by abiotic processes?

Up until now, I had been using a machine learning-based approach to flag instances of rain, which has not been a satisfying solution--i.e. using pattern matching to model the spectral signature of rain, and for any recording classified as containing rain, I had to discard the entire acoustic sample regardless of whether the rain event spanned the entire 1-minute acoustic sample or whether there was just a single frequency peak from an ephemeral rain drop. (Note: I was less successful in using this approach to identify instances of wind occupying acoustic space).

Instead, I'm hoping to find a signal processing approach to specifically target/filter out unwanted frequency peaks so that I don't have to discard the reams of hard-fought data "contaminated" by rain/wind (rain is no uncommon occurrence where I work in the tropics) in order to preserve as many of my recordings as possible.

I have a lot of data, so manual inspection (beyond validating a small subset) isn't a viable solution.

Thanks,

Danielle

messages.subject: Release of seewave 2.1.3
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (2.1.3) is on its way to CRAN.
Many thanks to Andrey Anikin, Thibaut Marin-Cudraz, Stuart Gage and Jens Piontkowski
Enjoy
Jerome

------
NEW FUNCTION
o lts(): long-term spectrogram, a function to produce a spectrogram over several survey files (obtained with a Wildlife Acoustics SongMeter recorder).

OTHER CHANGES
o dBweight(): returns now the ITU-R 468 noise weighting. Added by Andrey Anikin.
o dynspec(), meanspec(), spec(), spectro(), spectro3D(), wf(): the argument 'dB' can now take the value 'ITU' for the the ITU-R 468 noise weighting. Added by Andrey Anikin.
o env(), timer(): a new argument 'asmooth' for a smooth based on autocorrelation. By Thibaut Marin-Cudraz.
o ffilter(): a bug fixed when 'wave' is not a Wave object and when 'rescale=TRUE'
o listen(): a new argument, 'channel', to choose the channel to listen to.
o NDSI(): a new argument, 'max', to compute the maximum, rather than the sum, of the biophony frequency band. Thanks to Stuart Gage.
o sox(): improved by Andre Mikulec for a better OS implementation, new argument 'option' and 'shQuote_type'.
o spec(): bug fixed when dB!=NULL or dB!="max0". Thanks to Andrey Anikin.
o spectro(), oscillo(), oscilloST(): a new argument 'fastdisp' (by default FALSE) to speed up the graphic display of long sounds (with more than 20,000 samples). This also increases the display of all functions that include an oscillogram. Important: this new feature should be kept to FALSE to produce high-quality figures.
o stft.ext(): a .C code change following CRAN request.
 o timer(): the argument 'threshold' can now take a function so that the threshold can be defined according to the mean, median, standard deviation or any parameter describing the amplitude envelope. Thanks to Jens Piontkowski for the suggestion.

DEPRECATED & DEFUNCT
o stft.ext(): this function based on C code does not pass R CRAN check anymore.

--
